title: Keep partitions a manageable size
summary: A partition should not grow without a useful bound.
introduction: A partition should not grow without a useful bound. Your task: Name the partition values for Mia in November 2026.
learningObjectives: Name the partition values for Mia in November 2026.
Explain the example for keep partitions a manageable size

blocks.text: A partition should not grow without a useful bound. A time bucket can split a long history into smaller groups.
Use a local single-node Cassandra 4+ practice cluster and cqlsh. The SimpleStrategy keyspace below is only for that local lesson. These commands do not run in this site's SQLite playground.

blocks.code: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reading_by_month(reader_id text,month text,day date,title text,PRIMARY KEY((reader_id,month),day));
blocks.title: Keep partitions a manageable size

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: A primary key identifies a row and prevents duplicate key values. Related records can refer to that key.
In this CQL primary key, the inner parentheses name the partition key. Remaining key fields are clustering columns.

blocks.text: The partition key now combines a reader and a month, such as mia with 2026-11.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: The right bucket depends on real data size and queries. A month label is a modelling choice, not an automatic Cassandra feature.
